title: Hotpatch: oncall escalation - batcher lease regression and tenant-signal repair
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Customer escalation: multiple customers reported intermittent high tail latency and suppressed short-request throughput across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters during overlapping maintenance waves. Symptoms: short requests (<=64 tokens) experienced 10-30x latency spikes, long-context requests became 'sticky' in the continuous batcher, and queue depth metrics showed starvation rather than uniform backlog. Oncall saw surge alerts from two enterprise customers and initiated a P0 warroom.
reproduction_steps: Deploy runtime-1.19.2 with recent prefetch-quarantine and admission-smoothing flags enabled on a mixed-tenancy cluster.
Simulate mixed-length workload: 20% long-context (>=4096 tokens) streams at steady rate and 80% short requests as Poisson bursts.
Trigger rolling maintenance (drain/restart) on 2/3 hosts to reproduce lifecycle timing skew.
Observe batcher lease expiry handshake timing: short requests pile up while long-context in-progress batches hold KV locks for extended periods.
Capture metrics: batcher.admission.leases.*, queue.depth.*, kv.cache.hit_rate, rpc.latency.p50/p95/p99.
root_cause: Regression introduced in admission lease TTL calculation combined with a race in the prefetch-quarantine handshake. When hosts rejoin after maintenance, lease renewal backoff and quarantine expiration overlapped, allowing long-context batches to retain admission tokens and KV cache ownership for longer than intended; admission smoothing then suppressed new short-request admission windows, causing starvation.
mitigation_steps: Hotpatch rollout: runtime-1.19.3-hotfix increments admission lease TTL jitter boundaries and forces immediate lease revocation on host-rejoin to avoid stale ownership.
Add a prioritized preemption path for short requests that yields partial KV handoff without full eviction.
Oncall action: roll forward runtime-1.19.3-hotfix to affected clusters, and temporarily enable per-tenant shortflow-immortalize=false flag to restore velocity.
Customer communications: notify impacted customers with summary and expected mitigation ETA.
postmortem_actions: Write postmortem with timeline, root cause and customer impact.
Add deterministic lease renew unit tests and an integration test that simulates maintenance wave host churn with mixed-length traffic.
Instrument a new telemetry view: lease-ownership-duration by tenant + admission-window-starvation alerts.
Create an 'emergency-canary' gating job that runs the maintenance waveform scenario before large rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix successfully restores short-request p95 latency by at least 70% versus impacted baseline in staging.
Regression unit tests added and green in CI.
Rollout to 3 sample Dedicated customers and Hosted region us-west-2 without recurrence for 72h.
Postmortem reviewed and action items scheduled in next cycle.
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy runtime-1.19.3-hotfix to 2 non-production clusters and run maintenance waveform for 24h.
Staged rollout: apply to low-traffic Dedicated customers and one Hosted region during off-peak window.
Full rollout: roll across remaining regions and Dedicated pools with automated rollback policy if p99 latency or error budgets breach thresholds.
Communications: update status page and send customer emails at canary start and completion.
notes: Engineering triaged the issue during oncall rotation on 2025-06-22; initial rollback to 1.19.1 temporarily reduced but did not eliminate starvation.
Customer escalations elevated due to SLA impact; account team requested daily updates.
Test harness for maintenance-wave simulation created (repo: stress/maintenance-wave) and used to validate hotfix.
